question: How well does this test pick out the people who have the condition?

bossuyt2015.cite: Bossuyt et al. (2015). STARD 2015: an updated list of essential items for reporting diagnostic accuracy studies. BMJ 351: h5527.
bossuyt2015.checked: every quote read word for word in the vault's text copy of the PMC full text (library No. 282, PMC4623764) on 20 Nov 2026; the article is online-only (h5527), so places are given as STARD items, tables and the introduction; in-text reference numbers are left out of the quotes

steps.title: Recruit the suspected
steps.text: Take the people in whom the test would really be used: a consecutive series of those suspected of the condition, not a mix of the very sick and the plainly healthy.

quotes.text: Whether participants formed a consecutive, random, or convenience series

steps.title: Run the new test
steps.text: Apply the test under evaluation (the index test) to everyone, with its cut-off for a positive result fixed in advance.

quotes.where: table 3, the definition of index test

quotes.text: Definition of and rationale for test positivity cut-offs or result categories of the index test, distinguishing pre-specified from exploratory

steps.title: Reference standard
steps.text: Establish who really has the condition with the best method available, in everyone, not only in those who tested positive.

quotes.text: The best available method for establishing the presence or absence of the target condition; a gold standard would be an error-free reference standard

steps.title: Read blind
steps.text: Whoever reads one test must not know the other's result, or what they expect will colour what they see.

quotes.text: Whether clinical information and reference standard results were available to the performers or readers of the index test

steps.title: Count the 2 × 2
steps.text: Cross the two results in a table: true and false positives, false and true negatives. Sensitivity and specificity follow from its columns.

quotes.text: Cross tabulation of the index test results (or their distribution) by the results of the reference standard
Proportion of those with the target condition who test positive with the index test
Proportion of those without the target condition who test negative with the index test

spectrum-bias.text: if only healthy controls are included, the estimates of test accuracy may not reflect the performance of the test in clinical applications.

exercise.title: Move the cut-off
exercise.intro: Each person has a test value. Above the cut-off the test says positive. Move the cut-off and watch the 2 × 2 table, sensitivity and specificity trade against each other. Then swap the people without the condition: clinic patients with look-alike illnesses, or healthy volunteers.

quote.text: It is now well established that sensitivity and specificity are not fixed test properties.

exercise.data_label: Example data, made up for this exercise: 60 people with the condition and 140 without, test values drawn from bell curves with a fixed seed.

limits: STARD 2015 is a reporting guideline; it lists what a report must say rather than prescribing how to run the study. The steps follow its items.
The rapid antigen test example on the card is not worked through with real numbers here.
Predictive values and the ROC curve are mentioned by STARD but not shown.
